page: Amazon Web Services r8i.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. This x86_64 architecture system features 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes a large 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations.

In benchmark evaluations, the r8i.16xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core tests and the top 10% for Geekbench multi-core scores. Its memory subsystem achieves strong read-only bandwidth of 192.43 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. The system also excels in specialized tasks, scoring in the top 10% for software compilation and image processing. For database and key-value store workloads, it achieves 120.37 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks.

This instance does not include local storage, relying instead on network-attached storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of DDR5 memory relative to vCPUs makes it highly efficient for memory-bound applications without requiring excess compute allocation. The server is well-suited for in-memory databases, large-scale data processing, software compilation pipelines, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
